title: Clean the market price sheet
instructions:
## Real data is messy

The program input is a CSV of market prices collected by hand: `market,item,price_ghs`. Spaces, inconsistent capitals and missing prices (empty or `n/a`) are all in there.

## Do this

Read all lines from standard input (`sys.stdin`), skip the header, and for every row print `market,item,price` where the market is **title case**, the item is **lower case**, and the price is printed with two decimals or the word `missing`. Then print one summary line exactly like `valid: 3, missing: 2, average: 10.00` (the average of the valid prices, two decimals).

config.sampleInput:
market,item,price_ghs
 Makola , tomatoes , 12.5
Kejetia,Tomatoes,
makola,Onions,8
Kejetia , onions, 9.5
Takoradi,tomatoes,n/a

initialState.source:
import sys

lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
header = lines[0]
valid = []
missing = 0
for line in lines[1:]:
    market, item, price = [part.strip() for part in line.split(",")]
    # clean market and item, parse the price or count it missing, print the row

# print the summary

hints: str.title() and str.lower() fix the capitals; strip() removes the spaces.
try: value = float(price) except ValueError: it is missing. An empty string also fails float().

checks.message: Convert the price with float() inside a try/except.

realityNote: pandas does each of these steps in one call (str.strip, str.title, to_numeric with errors="coerce", mean), but every one of them hides a decision you just made explicitly: what counts as missing, and whether the average should include it.
